text:
support_jen: FYI - multiple customers reporting 503s during embedding-heavy workloads around 18:20 UTC. Ticket #CS-8732 attached. Errors look like gateway 503s coming back from upstream infer workers. sample log: `upstream: 503, reason: runner-exit`
sre_lin: I'm seeing a spike in worker restarts. Any recent deploys?
support_jen: no deploys in the last 2 hours. It started when they ramped concurrent embed requests (QPS ~3x). Customers report auth attempts timed out too.
sre_lin: alert from deploy_bot: `metric upstream_worker_restarts count +120 in 5m, p95 latency gateway +450ms` :warning:
deploy_bot: ALERT: hosted-infer-upstream-restarts - group=us-west - severity=high - link=https://ops.example/alerts/8271
ml_raj: attaching short repro we ran locally: stress-embed.sh --qps 800 --batch-size 128 against hosted/embeddings endpoint. After ~2m we see `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1) 79, GPU has fallen off the bus` in dmesg.
ingrid: that NVML Xid 79 indicates a GPU reset. Could be driver/firmware or memory corruption during heavy batch operations. Any kernel oops or segfaults?
sre_lin: collected `kubectl get pods -o wide` for the infer-node pool: several pods in CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 137 and the infer-runner container showing `SIGABRT` just before restart.
ml_raj: paste of /var/log/dmesg lines: ```[ 1223.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1) 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1223.456900] python3[2345]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f... sp 00007fff...
[ 1223.457001] kernel: oom-killer invoked for pid 2345 (infer-runner)
```
sre_lin: Confirmed GPU OOM + kernel-level resets. This matches container restarts -> gateway 503s. Might be NV driver noise combined with large batch allocations.
support_jen: customers also seeing auth timeouts; their token exchange tries hit the gateway and fail. CS team getting billing complaints because calls counted but returned 503.
ingrid: short-term mitigation options: 1) reduce max batch size for embeddings on hosted route (rollout to 0.75 of traffic) 2) enable fallback to quantized smaller model for embeddings for tiered customers 3) temporarily route heavy-embed customers to Dedicated pools if available.
sre_lin: I'm going to throttle incoming embed QPS at the gateway and set policy to drop batches >64. Doing a canary policy now for 10% of traffic to reduce pressure, then escalate.
deploy_bot: RUNBOOK STEP: set env EMBED_MAX_BATCH=64 on hosted-infer deployment. `kubectl set env deployment/hosted-infer EMBED_MAX_BATCH=64 -n hosted`
ml_raj: added repro note: the issue reproduces when prefix caching is cold and we allocate KV cache + large batch concurrently. Prefetch + large batch pushes vram past safe threshold on our GPU type (A100-40G).
sre_lin: collecting core dumps and requesting heap/profiles from affected pods. If someone from infra can snapshot the GPU state (nvidia-smi -q) and NVML logs, that will help root cause.
ingrid: commands for debug (paste to support engineer): ```# get recent container logs
kubectl logs pod/<pod> -c infer-runner --since=10m -n hosted
# collect dmesg and nvml
kubectl exec -it node/<node> -- dmesg | tail -n 50
kubectl exec -it node/<node> -- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER > /tmp/gpu-state.txt
# capture core (if core exists)
kubectl cp hosted/<pod>:/tmp/core.<pid> ./core.<pid>
```
support_jen: CS asked what we changed to mitigate billing hits. Can we apply a short-term credit or mark those requests not billable?
sre_lin: ops: we will mark calls that returned 503 with label `incident-7495550000` for manual billing review. I'll add a retention query in the billing pipeline.
ml_raj: next steps for root cause: 1) collect NVML logs and driver versions across nodes 2) test smaller batch profile + KV prefetch gating (only prefetch top-K prefixes) 3) run GPU mem-safety regression on our runtime with the same model and batch size to try to reproduce memory corruption.
deploy_bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance window proposed 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC for driver/firmware validation (requires node reboots). Please ack if ok.
support_jen: ack from CS. We told customers a mitigation ETA ~2 hours and offered credits pending billing review.
ingrid: I'll own the follow-up for firmware/drivers; sre_lin pls attach all collected logs to the incident page and tag infra.
sre_lin: attaching logs to https://incidents.example/7495550000 and pinging infra. If anyone sees a quick fix to avoid restarts (e.g., force smaller batch size rollback), call it out now.
support_jen: thanks everyone — CS will update customers. Will post final after billing flags applied. :thumbsup:
